title: The header guard that guards the wrong thing

prereqs.why: The bug is in a header guard, so you need to know what the preprocessor does with one.
The symptom is a one-definition-rule violation at link time, which is what the guard existed to prevent.

statement:
Two headers in a project. `shapes.h` was written first; `colours.h` was made by copying it and editing.

Including both in the same `.cpp` file produces a compiler error saying that nothing in `colours.h` exists — as though the file were empty.

Click the line that causes it.
hints: A header guard works by defining a macro the first time through and checking for it on later passes. What has to be true of the macro name for that to work across two different headers?
Read the three guard lines in `colours.h` carefully and compare them with the ones in `shapes.h`.
If `shapes.h` is included first, which macro is already defined by the time the preprocessor reaches `colours.h`?

payload.prompt: Click the line that causes the error.
